description: Build-host scaffold for Unity WebGL exports. The scaffold can't bundle the Unity editor output, so this family ships what you DO check in: a CI batch-mode build script, a Vite-based dev server to serve the built artifact, an index.html wired to the Unity loader, and a Build/ drop-zone for the editor's output. The Unity project itself lives elsewhere (source Assets/) and writes into Build/ via `Unity -batchmode`.

buildHints.whenToUse: Unity-authored games or interactive content that must ship as a browser-native WebGL build. This scaffold is the serving + CI harness — the Unity project source (Assets/, ProjectSettings/) lives in a separate repo or sibling directory, and the `Unity -batchmode` CLI writes its output into this repo's `Build/` directory. Pick godot-web or bevy-web if you haven't already committed to Unity.
firstSteps: Put your Unity editor build output in `Build/` — you need `Build.loader.js`, `Build.framework.js`, `Build.wasm`, `Build.data`, and optionally `Build.symbols.json` (filenames depend on the Unity product name in Player Settings).
Run locally: `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173 with the COOP/COEP headers Unity 2021 LTS+ needs for threads + SharedArrayBuffer.

CI build: `bash scripts/build-webgl.sh` — batch-mode Unity CLI incantation that runs a custom BuildScript and writes into `Build/`. Point `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH` at the Unity project source; `UNITY_VERSION` selects the Unity Hub-installed editor.
Ship: `pnpm build` runs Vite in production mode (`dist/`). The Build/ artifacts are static; any CDN works. Keep the COOP/COEP headers on the serving host.
For Unity Cloud Build or GitHub Actions, the same `scripts/build-webgl.sh` runs inside the Unity Docker image (`unityci/editor:ubuntu-<version>-webgl-<patch>`).
gotchas: Unity 2021.2+ WebGL builds enable threads by default, which requires the page to be served with `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`. Without these headers the loader fails with a SharedArrayBuffer error — Vite's server is configured here; make sure production hosting mirrors it.

Unity's Brotli-compressed output (`.br` files) requires the server to send `Content-Encoding: br`; gzip output needs `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Static hosts often strip this header, giving you a corrupted bundle. Either use Disabled compression in Player Settings or verify headers with `curl -I`.

The Unity loader filename depends on Player Settings → WebGL → Product Name. `index.html` here uses `Build/Build.loader.js` as a placeholder — rename on both sides after the first export so they match.
Batch-mode Unity must be activated and licensed (Personal/Pro/Plus) or it exits with code 12 after 30 days of trial. For CI, pre-activate with `-createManualActivationFile` + `-manualLicenseFile`.

WebGL builds have no multi-threaded GC — long GC pauses show up as freezes in JS profilers. Keep per-frame allocations minimal and profile with Unity's built-in profiler attached to the running WebGL page.
Output size: the data file (`Build.data`) often exceeds 50 MB even for simple games. Enable compression (Brotli for Cloudflare/Vercel; gzip for sites that can't set `Content-Encoding: br`).
architectureNotes: Treat this scaffold as pure infra — the Unity C# source is NOT here. Point `UNITY_PROJECT_PATH` at the Unity project (separate repo or sibling dir) and let `build-webgl.sh` drop output into `Build/`.
Unity's WebGL loader wants exclusive ownership of the canvas; do not decorate it with external CSS transforms (they're ignored on resize).

placeholders.description: Loads Unity's WebGL bootstrap from ./Build/Build.loader.js and starts the instance via createUnityInstance(). Update the loader URL and the Unity company/product metadata in the script block to match your editor Player Settings on first export.
Unity CLI batch-mode build script. Replace BuildScript.PerformWebGLBuild with your actual editor C# method (e.g. inside Assets/Editor/Build.cs) once the Unity project exists.
